National Government, its departments, bureaus, offices and agencies,
including State Universities and Colleges (SUCs); Government-Owned or
Controlled Corporations (GOCCs); Government Financial Institutions (GFI); and
Local Government Units (LGUs).
5 Attached as Annex "A" of this Circular is the prescribed template for a Call-Off.
6 Attached as Annex "B" of this Circular is the prescribed template for a Framework Agreement.
7 Attached as Annex "C" of this Circular is the prescribed template for a Framework Agreement List.

chunks.section: Section 4.3 - In order to ensure an open and transparent process, attract a broader pool of
chunks.text:
bidders to drive competitive pricing, diverse market ideas and innovative
solutions, and ultimately achieve value for money, Framework Agreement
requires the use of either Competitive Bidding or Limited Source Bidding as a
mode of procurement, as may be applicable. However, procurement projects
below the threshold amount of Two Million Pesos (PhP 2,000,000.00) for
Competitive Bidding may still use Framework Agreement as long as it follows
the procedure for Competitive Bidding.

chunks.section: Section 4.4 - The use of Framework Agreement as a procurement strategy is anchored on
chunks.text:
time and costs savings generated through the reduction of administrative
burden and cost of repetitive bidding. Moreover, PEs can leverage economies
of scale through bulk buying or consolidating procurement requirements in one
bidding, which likewise avoids splitting of contract. Of greater significance to
public procurement is the ability of a Framework Agreement to ensure supply
security and supply chain flexibility as well as mitigate compliance risks which
often hound PEs even with proper planning given the shifting market dynamics
and heterogenous bidder capacity.

chunks.section: Section 4.5 - Accordingly, Framework Agreement is best suited for the procurement of
chunks.text:
Goods, Infrastructure Projects or Consulting Services that are:
a.
frequently, routinely or repeatedly used;
b.
used for an indefinite period or quantity;
c.
needed over a long or set period but the exact quantity, timing or scope
of work or scope of service is unpredictable;
d.
by its nature, use or characteristics, the need arises on an urgent basis;
e.
needed for disaster preparedness and response; or
f.
other analogous or similar circumstances.

chunks.section: Section 5.1 - A Framework Agreement may be undertaken by a PE by setting up advance
chunks.text:
arrangements on what it will be procuring in the future and outlining the
technical specifications, scope of works, terms of reference, quantity or
volume, cost or pricing, delivery requirements or performance conditions and
such other terms and conditions over a set period governing future
procurement.

chunks.section: Section 5.2 - The Framework Agreement does not guarantee procurement but creates the
chunks.text:
structure for future procurement as needed through a Mini Competition or Call-
Offs. Hence, it shall be in the nature of an option contract between the PE, as
the offeree and the Qualified Bidder, as the offeror covering the right to buy
any of the items, works, or services in the Framework Agreement List within
a specified period.

chunks.section: Annex A - of GPPB Resolution No. 12-2026 dated 23 July 2026
Section 5.5 - In determining the items, works, or services to be included in the Framework
chunks.text:
Agreement List, the End-User or Implementing Unit shall consider all of its
requirements that will benefit
from
a
pre-arranged
procurement
structure, but where actual procurements are done on a needs basis.

chunks.section: Section 5.7 - The maximum quantity to be indicated in the Framework Agreement List shall
chunks.text:
reflect the maximum that the End-User or Implementing Unit may need during
the covered period taking into consideration current inventory, if any, and past
procurement and utilization data in order to ensure optimum use of resources
as well as time and cost savings.

d.
Optimization of the ABC through Call-Offs made at the time of actual need;

Advantage of a lean and just-in-time procurements; and
f.
Reduction of additional costs arising from procurement delay.

chunks.text:
a.
There are prospective bidders that are willing and capable of providing the

b.
The estimated prices per unit or scope that constitutes the ABC is

d.
The quantity, volume, scope of work, scope of service, as well as the

chunks.section: Section 6.4 - No procurement shall be undertaken unless it is in accordance with the
chunks.text:
approved Indicative or Final Annual Procurement Plan (APP) of the PE, as the
case may be8. The PE, in the preparation of its APP, shall include procurement
projects that will be covered by a Framework Agreement and attach the
corresponding Framework Agreement List.

chunks.section: Section 6.6 - In the case of a multi-year Framework Agreement, as the same is merely an
chunks.text:
option contract and the acceptance by the PE of the Qualified Bidder's offer
does not create a procurement contract but merely establishes a structure for
future procurements as the need arises, a MYCA9 is not required prior to
entering into such agreement. The PE shall nonetheless ensure that the
budget necessary for its annual programming for the year is included in its
approved budget. Hence, the amount of annual estimate or programming shall
be the basis of the ABC for each year that shall be indicated in the APP.
The ABC for the first year, as indicated in the APP and Framework Agreement
List, shall be the basis in determining the required amount of the Bidding
Documents Fee, Bid Security, Single Largest Completed Contract (SLCC), Net
Financial Contracting Capacity, and Protest Fee.

Guidelines on the Issuance of Multi-Year Contractual Authority (MYCA)".

chunks.section: Section 6.7 - The PE shall conduct procurement using either Competitive Bidding or Limited
chunks.text:
Source Bidding, including procurement projects below the threshold amount
of more than Two Million Pesos (PhP 2,000,000.00) for Competitive Bidding
but will be using Framework Agreement, in accordance with the relevant
provisions herein and of RA No. 12009 and its IRR.

chunks.text:
valid until such time as the execution of the Framework Agreement. For this
purpose, the BAC Secretariat shall request the bidder to extend its Bid Security
as may be necessary. Failure to extend the Bid Security shall disqualify the
bidder from further participating in the Framework Agreement.

If after publication, only one prospective bidder applies for eligibility check in accordance with the provisions of this IRR, and

b)
If after publication, more than one prospective bidder applies for eligibility check in accordance with the provisions of this IRR,

chunks.section: Section 6.12 - Notwithstanding the eligibility of the bidder, the BAC reserves the right to
chunks.text:
review its qualifications at any stage of the implementation of the Framework
Agreement. If there is any change in the capability of the bidder to undertake
its obligations under the Framework Agreement, as when it no longer meets
the eligibility criteria, the BAC shall revoke the eligibility of said bidder and
disqualify it from obtaining any award or contract. To ensure transparency, the
BAC shall inform the bidder of the reasons for its ineligibility prior to the
revocation.

chunks.section: Section 6.13 - Within five (5) calendar days from receipt by the bidder of the Notice to
chunks.text:
Execute a Framework Agreement, the bidder or its duly authorized
representative shall formally enter into a Framework Agreement with the PE.
The PE shall pay the bidder an amount of One Peso (Php 1.00) as a
consideration for the option granted to the PE to procure the Goods,
Infrastructure Projects, or Consulting Services covered in the Framework
Agreement List when the need arises.

chunks.section: Section 6.15 - Bidders may file a Protest before the HoPE against any decision of the BAC
chunks.text:
within seven (7) calendar days from receipt of said decision and after the denial
of its request for reconsideration, subject to the provisions of Section 83.2 of
the IRR of RA No. 12009 and other associated issuances.

chunks.section: Section 7.4 - A Framework Agreement shall contain the following stipulations
chunks.text:
a.
The Option Consideration shall be set at PHP 1.00 (One Peso).
b.
A fixed period of either one (1), two (2), or three (3) years within which
the PE may exercise its Option, reckoned from the time the Framework
Agreement was entered into and executed by the parties, and shall not
be subject to any extension.
c.
The perfection of the actual procurement contract shall be reckoned from
the date of execution of the Call-Offs.
d.
Upon the execution of the Call-Offs, all rules and guidelines governing
the implementation of procurement contracts under Section 71 of the RA
No. 12009 and its IRR shall be applicable.
e.
To guarantee the faithful performance by the supplier, contractor, or
service provider of its obligations under the Framework Agreement, the
supplier or service provider shall submit a Performance Securing
Declaration13 prior to the signing of the Framework Agreement. It shall
remain valid for the entire duration of the Framework Agreement
as prescribed in the Bidding Documents or until the final acceptance of
all items, works, or services indicated under the Framework Agreement
List subject to Items 8.2(b) and 9.6(a) hereof.
The prescribed template for the Performance Securing Declaration is
attached hereto for easy reference.
f.
A warranty security shall be required for each Call-Off, in the form and
amount stated in the Bidding Documents, and it shall remain valid for the
duration of the applicable warranty period in accordance with Section 90
of RA No. 12009 and its IRR.
g.
No modification of the provisions in the Framework Agreement shall
be allowed during its validity.

implementation of the Framework Agreement.

CIRCULAR NO. 02-2026
To

Subject
:
Guidelines on the Sale of Bidding Documents
1.0
POLICY STATEMENT
Pursuant to Section 47.4 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic
Act No. 12009, that upon submission of their bids, the Bidders shall pay the
applicable fee, if required. The Bidding Documents may also be secured from
the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) Secretariat upon payment of the
corresponding fee, if required. Bidders may be asked to pay a fee to recover
the cost for the preparation and development of the Bidding Documents, in
accordance with the guidelines to be issued by the Government Procurement
Policy Board (GPPB).
2.0
PURPOSE
These Guidelines provide the standard rates for the sale of Bidding Documents,
to rationalize the price, and to lessen the exercise of discretion by the Procuring
Entities (PEs) in order to avoid discouraging market participation and
competition.
3.0
SCOPE AND APPLICATION
3.1
These Guidelines shall apply to PEs or implementing units of all branches
and instrumentalities of the national government, its departments,
bureaus, offices and agencies, including State Universities and Colleges
(SUCs), Government-Owned or -Controlled Corporations (GOCCs),
Government Financial Institutions (GFIs), and Local Government Units
(LGUs).
3.2
The standard rate for the sale of Bidding Documents shall be applicable
in the procurement of Goods, Infrastructure Projects and Consulting
Services through modes of procurement using competitive selection.1
1 Competitive Bidding, Limited Source Bidding, Competitive Dialogue, and Unsolicited Offer with Bid Matching.

4.0

4.1
The concerned BAC shall make the Bidding Documents available from
the time the Invitation to Bid or Request for Expression of Interest was

4.2
The price of the Bidding Documents shall be included in the Invitation to
Bid or Request for Expression of Interest to inform all prospective
bidders.3
4.3
The BAC shall issue the Bidding Documents to any prospective bidder
upon payment of the standard rate of the Bidding Documents.
4.4
The PEs are proscribed from adopting any internal rule or practice that
establish prices that are inconsistent or beyond the standard rate for the
sale of Bidding Documents set forth in these Guidelines.
4.5
The proceeds from the sale of the Bidding Documents shall continue to
be used for the payment of honoraria and overtime pay as provided
under applicable budgeting rules and regulations or augment the funds
for the PE's legal assistance and indemnification package as provided in

1.0
POLICY STATEMENT

chunks.section: Section 1.1 - The Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act (RA)
chunks.text:
No. 12009 affirms the commitment of the Government of the Philippines
to promote the ideals of good governance with view towards transparency,
competitiveness,
efficiency,
proportionality,
accountability,
public
monitoring, procurement professionalization, sustainability, and value for
money in government procurement.1

chunks.section: Section 1.3 - Accordingly, when two or more bidders are post-qualified and declared as
chunks.text:
the Lowest Calculated Responsive Bidder (LCRB), Most Economically
Advantageous
Responsive
Bidder
(MEARB),
Most
Advantageous
Responsive Bidder (MARB), or Highest Rated and Responsive Bidder
(HRRB), the Procuring Entities (PEs) shall apply a tie-breaking method that
is non-discretionary, non-discriminatory, and based solely on chance.
2.0
PURPOSE
These Guidelines are issued to prescribe a uniform procedure for resolving
instances of tied bids in competitive procurement, consistent with the principles
of fairness, transparency, and accountability under RA No. 12009 and its IRR.
1 Section 2 of the IRR of RA No. 12009.

chunks.section: Annex C - of GPPB Resolution No. 08-2026 dated 19 February 2026 Page 2 of 2
chunks.text:
3.0
SCOPE AND APPLICATION
These Guidelines shall apply to all branches and instrumentalities of the national
government, its departments, bureaus, offices and agencies, including State
Universities and Colleges (SUCs), Government-Owned or -Controlled
Corporations (GOCCs), Government Financial Institutions (GFIs), and
Local Government Units (LGUs).
4.0
GENERAL GUIDELINES
4.1
The PEs shall adopt measures to resolve cases of a tie after post-
qualification among bidders determined and declared as LCRB, MEARB,
MARB, or HRRB.
4.2
At the onset of the bidding process, the PEs are required to identify and
specify in the Bidding Documents, as instruction or a matter of
information to prospective bidders, a ready and clear measure to be used
in the event two or more bidders have been post-qualified as LCRB,
MEARB, MARB or HRRB. In all cases, the measure determined by the PE
shall be non-discretionary and non-discriminatory such that the same is
based on sheer luck or chance. The PE may use "draw lots" or similar
methods of chance.
4.3
In lieu of the pre-determined criteria set in the Bidding Documents, the
PE may require the concerned bidders to agree on alternative selection
criteria, at the same day as the bid opening and evaluation, or on a later
date specifically scheduled by the PE for this purpose. The agreed
selection criteria shall be non-discretionary/non-discriminatory and is
similarly based on sheer luck or chance.
5.0
REPEALING CLAUSE
All guidelines and issuances, or any parts thereof, that are contrary to
or inconsistent with the provisions of these Guidelines are hereby
repealed, modified, or amended accordingly.
6.0
EFFECTIVITY
These Guidelines shall take effect fifteen (15) days after publication in the
Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation.
7.0
For compliance.
KIM ROBERT C. DE LEON
Chairperson
SGD.

Commission on Audit Auditors; and All Others Concerned
Subject
:
Guidelines on the Procurement of Printing Services
1.0
POLICY STATEMENT
All agencies of the government shall engage the services of the National
Printing Office (NPO), Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), and APO Production
Unit as Recognized Government Printers (RGPs) for the printing of accountable
forms and sensitive, high quality or high volume requirements, subject to the
following:
a. The RGPs shall undertake the printing requirements themselves and
shall not sub-contract any portion thereof to other printers; and
b. An agency may be allowed to engage private printers for the printing of
accountable forms and sensitive, high quality or high volume
requirements upon certification by the RGPs that they are unable to
service the said requirements. Said engagement of private printers shall
be in accordance with existing government procurement laws, rules, and
regulations.1
2.0
PURPOSE
These Guidelines aim to establish a uniform framework for the procurement of
printing services in government, ensuring compliance with Republic Act (RA)
No. 12009, or the "New Government Procurement Act," and its Implementing
Rules and Regulations (IRR), while safeguarding the integrity, security, and
quality of the printed materials.
1 For Fiscal Year (FY) 2026, the policy is covered by Section 25 (Printing Expenditures) General Provisions of the FY 2026
General Appropriations Act.

chunks.section: Annex B - of GPPB Resolution No. 08-2026 dated 19 February 2026 Page 2 of 3
chunks.text:
3.0
SCOPE AND APPLICATION
3.1
These Guidelines shall apply to the procurement of printing services by
Procuring Entities (PEs) or Implementing Units of all branches and
instrumentalities of the national government, its departments, bureaus,
offices and agencies, including State Universities and Colleges (SUCs),
Government-Owned or -Controlled Corporations (GOCCs), Government
Financial Institutions (GFIs), and Local Government Units (LGUs).
3.2
It shall not apply to official ballots and election paraphernalia, including
statement of votes, certificates of canvass, and paper seals, which is
covered by Section 184 of Batas Pambansa Blg. 881, otherwise known
as the Omnibus Election Code of the Philippines and Section 13 of
RA No. 9369.2
4.0
DEFINITION OF TERMS
For the purpose of these Guidelines, the following terms shall have the
corresponding meanings:
a. Accountable Forms. Refer to forms that are individually identified,
accounted for, and afforded appropriate security. The classification of
Accountable Forms shall be determined, maintained, and updated by the
competent oversight authority in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and
regulations.
b. Recognized Government Printers (RGPs). Refer to printers, namely,
NPO, BSP, and APO Production Unit, acknowledged by the government to
undertake the printing of accountable forms and sensitive, high quality or
high volume requirements.3
c. Sensitive, High Quality or High Volume Requirements. Refer to
printing requirements that are either sensitive in nature and demand high
quality or high volume printed materials, as determined by the PE.
5.0
PROCEDURE
5.1
All procurement of printing services shall be included in the PE's Annual
Procurement Plan.
5.2
The PE shall determine whether a printing services is for an accountable
form or for a sensitive, high quality or high volume document.
2 An Act Amending Republic Act No. 8436, Entitled "An Act Authorizing the Commission on Elections to Use an Automated Election
System in the May 11, 1998 National or Local Elections and in Subsequent National and Local Electoral Exercises, to Encourage
Transparency, Credibility, Fairness and Accuracy of Elections, Amending for the Purpose Batas Pambansa Blg. 881, as Amended,
Republic Act No. 7166 and Other Related Elections Laws, Providing Funds Therefor and for Other Purposes"
3 Sec.

chunks.section: Annex B - of GPPB Resolution No. 08-2026 dated 19 February 2026 Page 3 of 3
chunks.text:
5.3
The PE shall prepare the technical specifications for the accountable
forms or sensitive, high quality or high volume requirements, which shall
include, among others, the prescribed security features, output quantity,
and target completion time.
5.4
It shall then conduct a market scoping to determine the Approved
Budget for the Contract taking into consideration the prevailing standard
cost for its printing requirements.
5.5
The PE shall engage the services of RGPs, namely: NPO, BSP, and APO
Production Unit, for the printing of accountable forms and sensitive, high
quality or high volume requirements.
5.6
Should the PE determine that a capable RGP is available to undertake
printing services, the PE shall send a Request for Quotation to the
RGPs. The quotations received will be evaluated by the PE to determine
which among the RGPs is most capable of performing the printing
services in the most advantageous terms for the government.
5.7
The appropriate RGP engaged by the PE shall directly undertake the
printing services for the contracts entered into, and cannot engage,
subcontract, or assign any private printer to undertake the performance
of the printing services or any portion thereof.
5.8
The PE may engage private printers for the printing of accountable forms
and sensitive, high quality or high volume requirements upon
certification by the RGPs that they are unable to service the said
requirements. Said engagement of private printers shall be in
accordance with existing government procurement laws, rules, and
regulations.
6.0
REPEALING CLAUSE
All guidelines and issuances, or any parts thereof, that are contrary to
or inconsistent with the provisions of these Guidelines are hereby
repealed, modified, or amended accordingly.
7.0
EFFECTIVITY
These Guidelines shall take effect fifteen (15) days after publication in the
Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation.
8.0
For compliance.
KIM ROBERT C. DE LEON
Chairperson
SGD.

Subject
:
Guidelines on the Resolution of Tied Bids through
Tie-Breaking Method
1.0
POLICY STATEMENT

chunks.section: Section 1.1 - The Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act (RA)
chunks.text:
No. 12009 affirms the commitment of the Government of the Philippines
to promote the ideals of good governance with view towards transparency,
competitiveness,
efficiency,
proportionality,
accountability,
public
monitoring, procurement professionalization, sustainability, and value for
money in government procurement.1

chunks.section: Section 1.3 - Accordingly, when two or more bidders are post-qualified and declared as
chunks.text:
the Lowest Calculated Responsive Bidder (LCRB), Most Economically
Advantageous
Responsive
Bidder
(MEARB),
Most
Advantageous
Responsive Bidder (MARB), or Highest Rated and Responsive Bidder
(HRRB), the Procuring Entities (PEs) shall apply a tie-breaking method that
is non-discretionary, non-discriminatory, and based solely on chance.
2.0
PURPOSE
These Guidelines are issued to prescribe a uniform procedure for resolving
instances of tied bids in competitive procurement, consistent with the principles
of fairness, transparency, and accountability under RA No. 12009 and its IRR.
1 Section 2 of the IRR of RA No. 12009.

chunks.section: Annex C - of GPPB Resolution No. 08-2026 dated 19 February 2026 Page 2 of 2
chunks.text:
3.0
SCOPE AND APPLICATION
These Guidelines shall apply to all branches and instrumentalities of the national
government, its departments, bureaus, offices and agencies, including State
Universities and Colleges (SUCs), Government-Owned or -Controlled
Corporations (GOCCs), Government Financial Institutions (GFIs), and
Local Government Units (LGUs).
4.0
GENERAL GUIDELINES
4.1
The PEs shall adopt measures to resolve cases of a tie after post-
qualification among bidders determined and declared as LCRB, MEARB,
MARB, or HRRB.
4.2
At the onset of the bidding process, the PEs are required to identify and
specify in the Bidding Documents, as instruction or a matter of
information to prospective bidders, a ready and clear measure to be used
in the event two or more bidders have been post-qualified as LCRB,
MEARB, MARB or HRRB. In all cases, the measure determined by the PE
shall be non-discretionary and non-discriminatory such that the same is
based on sheer luck or chance. The PE may use "draw lots" or similar
methods of chance.
4.3
In lieu of the pre-determined criteria set in the Bidding Documents, the
PE may require the concerned bidders to agree on alternative selection
criteria, at the same day as the bid opening and evaluation, or on a later
date specifically scheduled by the PE for this purpose. The agreed
selection criteria shall be non-discretionary/non-discriminatory and is
similarly based on sheer luck or chance.
5.0
REPEALING CLAUSE
All guidelines and issuances, or any parts thereof, that are contrary to
or inconsistent with the provisions of these Guidelines are hereby
repealed, modified, or amended accordingly.
6.0

These Guidelines shall take effect fifteen (15) days after publication in the
Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation.
7.0
For compliance.
KIM ROBERT C. DE LEON
Chairperson
SGD.

Subject
:
Guidelines for Legal Assistance and Indemnification
Package of Bids and Awards Committee Members and its
Support Staff
1.0
POLICY STATEMENT
1.1.
Consistent with the government's commitment of safeguarding
procurement practitioners, all members of the Bids and Awards
Committee (BAC), Technical Working Group (TWG), and Secretariat shall
be entitled to private legal assistance and indemnification package
pursuant to Sections 106 and 107 of Republic Act (RA) No. 12009 and its
Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR).
1.2.
All members of the BAC, TWG and Secretariat are authorized to engage
the services of private lawyers or external counsel, immediately upon
receipt of notice of administrative, civil or criminal action, suit or
proceeding filed against them in connection with the performance of their
functions and duties. The lawyer's fee shall be part of the indemnification
package for the members of the BAC, TWG, and Secretariat, subject to
the provisions of Section 107 of RA No. 12009 and its IRR.1
1.3.
Under Section 107 of RA No. 12009 and its IRR, the Government
Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) shall establish an equitable
indemnification package for public officials and employees providing
services in the BAC, TWG, and Secretariat. Such indemnification package
may be in the form of free legal assistance, liability insurance, and other
forms of protection and indemnification for all costs and expenses
reasonably incurred by such persons in connection with any
administrative, civil or criminal action, suit or proceeding to which they
may be, or have been made, a party by reason of the performance of
1 Section 106 of RA No. 12009 and its IRR.

chunks.section: Annex D - of GPPB Resolution No. 08-2026 dated 19 February 2026 Page 2 of 6
chunks.text:
their functions or duties, unless they are finally adjudged in such action
or proceeding to be liable for gross negligence or grave misconduct or
grave abuse of discretion.
2.0
PURPOSE
These Guidelines are formulated to prescribe the rules and procedures in
granting legal assistance and indemnification to the BAC members and BAC
Support Staff pursuant to Sections 106 and 107 of RA No. 12009 and its IRR.
3.0
DEFINITION OF TERMS
a. BAC. Refers refers to the Committee established in accordance with

chunks.section: Article V - of RA No. 12009
chunks.text:
b. BAC Members. Refer to the regular and provisional members of the
BAC determined in accordance with Section 41 of RA No. 12009 and its
IRR.
c. BAC Support Staff. Refers to the members of the BAC Secretariat and
the TWG duly designated by the PE pursuant to the provisions of Rule V
of the IRR of RA No. 12009.
d. Indemnification. Refers to the assistance or remuneration given to the
members of the BAC and/or other BAC Support Staff for any loss,
damage, or injury caused to them by reason of the lawful performance
of their duties.
e. Private Legal Assistance. Refers to the services of a private lawyer or
external counsel engaged by or on behalf of the members of the BAC
and/or the BAC Support Staff resulting from the filing of any criminal or
civil action or proceedings against the BAC member or BAC Support Staff
for acts made in connection with the lawful performance of their
functions.
f. Liability Insurance. Refers to the insurance policy purchased and
maintained by the Procuring Entity (PE) in favor of a member of the BAC
and/or the BAC Support Staff against any liability asserted against or
incurred by the person in any such capacity or arising out of the person's
status as such.
g. Medical Assistance. The remuneration given by the PE for any injury
or disability incurred by members of the BAC and/or the BAC Support
Staff in the lawful performance of their official functions and duties. For
this purpose, "injury" means any impairment arising from and in the
course of procurement-related activities.

chunks.section: Annex D - of GPPB Resolution No. 08-2026 dated 19 February 2026 Page 3 of 6
chunks.text:
4.0
SCOPE AND APPLICATION
4.1
These Guidelines shall apply to PEs or implementing units of all branches
and instrumentalities of the national government, its departments,
bureaus, offices and agencies, including State Universities and Colleges
(SUCs), Government-Owned or -Controlled Corporations (GOCCs),
Government Financial Institutions (GFIs), and Local Government Units
(LGUs).
4.2
In the event of settlement or compromise, indemnification shall be
limited solely to matters covered by the settlement, subject to the
approval of the Head of the Procuring Entity (HoPE) and upon the
recommendation of the Legal Service/Division/Unit or a committee
created for the purpose, based on records of the case and other
supporting documents, that the person to be indemnified has not
committed gross negligence, misconduct, or grave abuse of discretion in
the performance of their duties and functions, pursuant to Section 107
of RA No. 12009 and its IRR.
5.0
GENERAL CONDITIONS
5.1
Free Legal Assistance

chunks.section: Section 5.1.1 - The PE shall, to the fullest extent permitted by these Guidelines,
chunks.text:
indemnify a BAC member and/or any of the BAC Support Staff
who, in the performance of their official functions, becomes a
party to a pending or completed civil, criminal, or administrative
action. Consistent with Section 106 of RA No. 12009 and its IRR,
the concerned BAC member or BAC Support Staff may engage the
services of a private lawyer or external counsel upon receipt of
notice that an action or proceeding has been initiated against
them, the lawyer's fee shall form part of the indemnification
package.

chunks.section: Section 5.1.4 - The free legal assistance shall not cover
chunks.text:
a. any action or suit initiated by a BAC member or BAC Support
Staff in his personal capacity or on behalf of the PE, unless
such action, proceedings, or claim was authorized by the HoPE
or the authorized approving authority; or
b. any action or suit initiated by the Government against the BAC
member or BAC Support Staff.

chunks.section: Section 5.1.5 - The BAC member or BAC Support Staff shall be entitled to actual,
chunks.text:
moral, and exemplary damages when awarded by the court.
Likewise, the attorney representing the BAC member or BAC
Support Staff shall be entitled to attorney's fees awarded by the
court.
5.2
Liability Insurance

chunks.section: Section 5.2.2 - The liability insurance policy shall cover only those liabilities
chunks.text:
asserted against the public official and incurred by them in their
capacity as BAC member or BAC Support Staff, as the case may
be.
Provided that such BAC member or BAC Support Staff shall not be
adjudged in such action or proceedings to be guilty of gross
negligence, gross misconduct, or grave abuse of discretion or
guilty of any other complaint or charges.

chunks.section: Section 5.2.4 - For purposes of this issuance, the term "loss" shall include
chunks.text:
judgments, expenses for settlement or compromise, as well as all
reasonable fees and other expenses incurred by the public official
or employee in their capacity as BAC member or BAC Support
Staff, in connection with any administrative, civil, or criminal
action, suit or proceeding to which they may be or have been

chunks.section: Section 5.3.2 - The claimant(s) shall be entitled to indemnification for any injury
chunks.text:
or disability resulting from the actual performance or while
undertaking their official functions as defined by law and without
any contributory negligence on their part. Provided further, that
they exercised due diligence to prevent harm or injury to
themselves. The claimant or his/her relatives must notify the HoPE
within seven (7) calendar days from the occurrence of the injury
or disability.

chunks.section: Section 5.3.3 - The medical assistance herein provided shall consist of
chunks.text:
indemnification for medicines, laboratory and hospitalization
expenses, provided that the amount claimed shall not exceed the
actual amount incurred, substantiated by receipts and other
supporting documents.

chunks.section: Section 5.3.4 - Indemnification shall only be made upon presentation of proof of
chunks.text:
payment in connection with the injury or disability suffered.
6.0
PROCEDURE FOR GRANTING ASSISTANCE AND INDEMNIFICATION
OF BAC MEMBERS
6.1
The claimant(s) shall file their respective claim(s) for legal assistance,
liability insurance, or medical assistance as the case may be, with the
HoPE.
6.2
The HoPE shall be given at least fifteen (15) to thirty (30) calendar days
to examine, review, verify and validate the authenticity of the documents
presented by the claimant.
6.3
Upon finding that all the requirements have been duly complied with and
that all the necessary documents submitted are genuine, the HoPE shall
authorize the processing of the claims and the corresponding payment

chunks.section: Annex D - of GPPB Resolution No. 08-2026 dated 19 February 2026 Page 6 of 6
chunks.text:
in accordance with applicable accounting and auditing rules and
regulations.
6.4
Any expense, such as attorney's fees and other legal fees, liability
insurance, and medical expenses, incurred in advance by the claimant,
and arising from the performance of official functions in such capacity,
shall be subject to reimbursement upon submission of the necessary
documents and approval thereof by the HoPE.
6.5
If found guilty of gross negligence, gross misconduct, or grave abuse of
discretion, the concerned BAC member or BAC staff shall return any
monetary assistance released for their respective claim(s) for legal
assistance, liability insurance, or medical assistance through salary
deductions or through cash payment.
7.0
FUNDING SOURCE
The funds to be used for the grant of the free legal assistance, liability insurance
or medical assistance shall be charged against the Agency's available budget for
Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE) under its annual
appropriation.
Protest fees, proceeds from the sale of bidding documents, and any other
additional funds derived from other income-generating activities of the agency
may be used to augment the funding source provided in this Section.
8.0
REPEALING CLAUSE
All guidelines and issuances, or any parts thereof, that are contrary to
or inconsistent with the provisions of these Guidelines are hereby
repealed, modified, or amended accordingly.
9.0
EFFECTIVITY
These Guidelines shall take effect fifteen (15) days after publication in the
Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation.

Subject

for

for

1.0
POLICY STATEMENT

chunks.section: Section 1.1 - The State shall give priority to science and technology to accelerate social
chunks.text:
progress and national development, among others.1 Furthermore, it shall
give priority to research and development, invention, innovation, and their
utilization, and to science and technology education, training, and services.2

chunks.section: Section 1.2 - To help stimulate innovation in the country, Republic Act (RA) No. 120093
chunks.text:
and RA No. 112934 mandate the Government Procurement Policy Board
(GPPB) and the National Innovation Council (NIC) to develop procurement
policies encompassing the entire research, innovation, and enterprise
ecosystem that shall ensure efficiency, transparency, timeliness, and
relevance in the procurement process, and to foster innovation, relevant
government agencies shall expedite the release of goods used in and
documents necessary for science, technology, and innovation (STI).5
1 Article II, Section 17 of the 1987 Constitution of the Philippines. The State shall give priority to education, science and technology,
arts, culture, and sports to foster patriotism and nationalism, accelerate social progress, and promote total human liberation and
development.
2 Article XIV, Section 10 of the 1987 Constitution of the Philippines. Science and technology are essential for national development
and progress. The State shall give priority to research and development, invention, innovation, and their utilization; and to science
and technology education, training, and services. It shall support indigenous, appropriate, and self-reliant scientific and
technological capabilities, and their application to the country's productive systems and national life.
3 The "New Government Procurement Act."
4 The "Philippine Innovation Act."
5 Section 37, RA No. 12009 provides, among others, that "[t]he GPPB, in coordination with the National Innovation Council (NIC),
shall develop procurement policies encompassing the entire research, innovation, and enterprise ecosystem. To foster innovation,
relevant government agencies shall expedite the release of goods used in and documents necessary for science, technology, and
innovation."
Section 26, RA No. 11293 provides, among others, that "[t]o help stimulate innovation in the country, the NIC shall coordinate
with the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) and its technical support office for the development and issuance of
public procurement guidelines, as authorized under Republic Act No. 9184 and its IRR [xxx]. The guidelines to be issued by the
NIC, in coordination with the GPPB for this purpose, shall ensure efficiency, transparency, timeliness and relevance in the
procurement process."

chunks.section: Annex A - of GPPB Resolution No. 04-2026, dated 15 January 2026
chunks.text:
Page 2 of 12
2.0
PURPOSE
These Guidelines are issued pursuant to Section 37 of the Implementing Rules
and Regulations (IRR) of RA No. 12009, which provides that Procuring Entities
(PEs) may procure goods and services directly from a legally, technically, and
financially capable manufacturer or supplier, or from a qualified startup
business.6
3.0
DEFINITION OF TERMS
The following terms, words, and phrases shall be understood as follows:
a. Direct Procurement for STI - A mode of procurement where covered
entities under these Guidelines may directly procure Research and
Development (R&D) or STI goods and services from a qualified
manufacturer, supplier, or startup business, as defined in these Guidelines.
b. Early Adopter - A PE that is among the first to procure or utilize a new or
significantly improved product, service, or process prior to its widespread
adoption in the market, including the procurement of pre-commercial goods
and services.7
c. Early Market Engagement - The proactive, collaborative, and strategic
process involving organized interactions between a buyer and potential
suppliers, service providers, or the market at large, with the primary aim of
stimulating the development of innovative goods and services that meet
specific needs.8
d. Foreign Supplier - A citizen of a foreign country or an entity in which
Filipino ownership or interest is less than sixty percent (60%), engaged in
the manufacture or sale of the goods, or performance of the general
services being procured.
6 Direct Procurement for Science, Technology and Innovation is a mode of procurement where the Procuring Entity may procure
the following goods and services directly from a legally, technically, and financially capable manufacturer or supplier, or from a
qualified startup business:
a)
Supplies, materials, equipment, and related services to be used actually, exclusively, and directly in the conduct of
research and development projects or activities;
b)
Goods which include products of a commissioned task by a Procuring Entity which were processed, developed, and
manufactured in satisfaction of its needs and requirements.

chunks.section: Annex A - of GPPB Resolution No. 04-2026, dated 15 January 2026
chunks.text:
These include: (i) pre-commercial goods and services that
involve early market engagement to stimulate the development of new goods and services that meet specific
government needs; and (ii) goods to be manufactured by qualified startup businesses alongside the thrust to develop
and support new and startup businesses. Unless otherwise indicated in a written agreement, the intellectual property
rights and ownership over the commissioned goods developed and manufactured pursuant to this provision shall belong
to the Procuring Entity, and no manufacturing or sale thereof can be performed by the supplier; and
c)
Other goods analogous to the foregoing. [xxx]
7 European Commission (2021). Commission Notice - Guidance on Innovation Procurement.
8 World Bank - Operations Policy and Country Services (2025). Early Market Engagement Fact Sheet.

chunks.section: Annex A - of GPPB Resolution No. 04-2026, dated 15 January 2026
chunks.text:
Page 3 of 12
e. Innovation - The creation of new ideas that results in the development of
new or improved policies, products, processes, or services which are then
spread or transferred across the market.9
f. Innovative Goods and Services - New or significantly improved
products, services, processes, technical specifications or components,
methods, and tools that enhance the government's ability to deliver
services.10
g. Pre-commercial Goods and Services - Innovative goods and services
in the stage of prototype validation, pilot production, or early development
stage but have yet to be widely available as commercial or market-ready
goods and services. As applicable, these shall have regulatory or standards
compliance appropriate to their development stage 11 and must be
supported by documentation demonstrating ownership of or authority to
use the underlying technology, including pending, registered, or otherwise
documented Intellectual Property (IP) or technology rights, as required
under these guidelines, applicable laws, and/or the needs of the PE.
h. Qualified Manufacturer and Supplier - A manufacturer, supplier, trader,
distributor, importer, or service provider, which meets all the following
eligibilities:
i.
Financial Eligibility - the capacity to manufacture, distribute, or
deliver the goods or services covered under Section 4.2 of these
Guidelines.
ii.
Legal Eligibility - the capacity to act as an entity as evidenced by
permits, licenses, and/or registrations required by law to engage in
the business of manufacturing, distributing, or delivering the goods
or services being procured.
iii.
Technical Eligibility - the experience or expertise to undertake the
services, manufacturing, distribution, or delivery of the goods or
services being procured.
9 Section 3 (f) of RA No. 11293.
10 Section 3 (k) of RA No. 11293.
11 These may include, but are not limited to, License to Operate issued by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Health
Technology Assessment issued by the Department of Health (DOH), Product Certification or Philippine Standard Mark issued by
the Bureau of Philippine Standards of the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI-BPS), Type Acceptance/Approval Certificate
issued by the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC), or proof of inclusion in a regulatory sandbox program by a
relevant regulatory body.

chunks.section: Annex A - of GPPB Resolution No. 04-2026, dated 15 January 2026
chunks.text:
Page 4 of 12
i.
Qualified Startup Business - Any business entity duly registered in the
Philippines,12 and operating for more than one (1) year but not more than
five (5) years from its registration. It must fall under any of the micro, small,
and medium enterprise categories provided under Section 3 of RA No. 6977,
as amended,13 and be engaged in the creation, development, production,
or commercialization of innovative products, processes, or services through
the application for, or commercial exploitation of, IP rights such as patents,
utility models, and industrial designs.
j. Research and Development - Any activity which is a systematic,
intensive study directed toward greater knowledge or understanding of the
subject studied. This may include a systematic study directed specifically
toward applying new knowledge to meet a recognized need, or a systematic
application of knowledge toward the production of useful materials, devices,
and systems or methods, including design, development, and improvement
of prototypes and new processes to meet specific requirements.14
k. Related Services - These involve activities such as installation, calibration,
surveying, testing and analytical services, maintenance, and repair. These
also include systematic and creative work undertaken in STI, higher
education and training, scientific services, and marketing or promotional
activities for STI outputs, among others.
l. Science, Technology, and Innovation - The interconnected and
mutually reinforcing activities encompassing the development and testing
of theories to describe the natural and social phenomena (science), the
practical use of discoveries through technical methods, systems, devices,
skills, and practices (technology), and the implementation of new or
improved products, processes, or organizational methods that differ
significantly from previous ones and are brought into use or made available
to users (innovation).15
4.0
SCOPE AND COVERAGE

chunks.section: Section 4.1 - This Circular shall apply to PEs or implementing units of all branches and
chunks.text:
instrumentalities of the national government, its departments, bureaus,
offices and agencies, including State Universities and Colleges (SUCs),
Government-Owned and/or -Controlled Corporations (GOCCs), Government
Financial Institutions (GFIs), and Local Government Units (LGUs), provided
they meet at least one of the following:
12 As certified by the DTI, Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), DOST, or the NIC, as may be
applicable, pursuant to Section 76.1 (f) of the IRR of RA No. 12009.
13 The "Magna Carta for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises."
14 Section 3 (f), RA No. 11337, otherwise known as the "Innovative Startup Act."
15 OECD, Frascati Manual 2015: Guidelines for Collecting and Reporting Data on Research and Experimental Development;
OECD/Eurostat, Oslo Manual 2018: Guidelines for Collecting, Reporting and Using Data on Innovation, 4th Ed.

chunks.section: Section 4.1.2 - The PE has approved appropriations under the "Survey, Research,
chunks.text:
Exploration, and Development Expenses," explicitly stated and
detailed in the object of expenditures of its approved appropriations
in the General Appropriations Act (GAA), Local Expenditure Program
(LEP) or Corporate Operating Budget, as the case may be.

chunks.section: Section 4.2.1 - Supplies, materials, equipment, and Related Services to be used
chunks.text:
actually, exclusively, and directly in the conduct of R&D projects or
activities, including those undertaken for the research, development,
testing, or deployment of an STI program, activity, or project and
mandate.

chunks.section: Section 4.2.2.2 - Goods and services under this Section include
chunks.text:
a. Pre-commercial goods and services that involve early
market engagement to stimulate the development of
new goods and services that meet specific government
needs, wherein the PE intends to serve as an early
adopter or co-developer, supporting the testing,
validation, or initial development of goods and services
16 Consulting Services refer to services for Infrastructure Projects and other types of projects or activities of the government
requiring adequate external technical and professional expertise that are beyond the capability or capacity of the government to
undertake, such as, but not limited to: (1) advisory and review services; (2) pre-investment or feasibility studies; (3) design;
(4) construction supervision; (5) management and related services; and (6) other legal and technical services or special studies.

chunks.section: Annex A - of GPPB Resolution No. 04-2026, dated 15 January 2026
chunks.text:
Page 6 of 12
that is new to the local market and possess substantially
novel characteristics prior to their full commercialization,
provided that there is written justification from the PE
that the goods and services meet the specific needs of
the government with attached reference/s and provided
that any of the following documents are submitted:
(1) proof of freedom to operate, or documents that
establish that the goods and services can be freely
commercialized
in
the
country,
(2)
proof
of
registration/certification with the Intellectual Property
Office of the Philippines (IPOPHL); (3) proof of
application with the IPOPHL for registration or
certification.
b. Acquisition of goods to be manufactured by qualified
startup businesses alongside the thrust to develop and
support new and startup businesses.

chunks.section: Section 4.2.3 - Other goods analogous to the foregoing, which include but are not
chunks.text:
limited to:
a. Goods and services that directly support or complement
transaction activities across different stages of STI activities,
including, but not limited to, clinical testing, market validation,
market testing, biologicals production, etc.; provided that such
activities result in tangible outputs or data integral to the
development,
validation,
or
commercialization
of
pre-commercial goods or services; or
b. Other items deemed related or complementary to STI goods
and services, which may include emerging technologies and
hybrid innovations that are not yet formally recognized or
categorized under existing procurement classifications but are
anticipated to be mainstreamed in the future.
5.0
BIDDING FROM FOREIGN SOURCES
5.1
As provided under Sections 7817 and 79.118 of the IRR of RA No. 12009,
goods and/or services may be obtained from foreign sources, and the
procurement thereof shall be open to all eligible suppliers,
manufacturers, and distributors, with due priority and preference given
to Philippine products and services at all levels of the procurement
process, including raw material, ingredients, supplies, or fixtures.
17 Consistent with the country's obligations under treaty or international or executive agreement, Goods may be obtained from
domestic or foreign sources and the procurement thereof shall be open to all eligible suppliers, manufacturers, and distributors.
18 The Procuring Entity shall give priority and preference to Philippine products and services. The preference and priority for

GPPB Resolution No. 17-2026 dated 14 August 2026 Page 1 of 10
RESOLUTION NO. 17-2026
APPROVING THE GUIDELINES ON THE PROCUREMENT FOR DISASTER
PREPAREDNESS, ANTICIPATORY MEASURES, AND DISASTER-RELATED MITIGATION
RESPONSE, RELIEF, RECOVERY, REHABILITATION, RECONSTRUCTION AND OTHER
ACTIVITIES, MEASURES, INTERVENTIONS AND EFFORTS TO PROTECT LIVES,
PROPERTY, VITAL PUBLIC SERVICES, INFRASTRUCTURE FACILITIES AND OTHER
PUBLIC UTILITIES
WHEREAS, Republic Act (RA) No. 12009, otherwise known as the "New Government
Procurement Act," took effect on 13 August 2024, while its Implementing Rules and Regulations
(IRR) took effect on 25 February 2025;
WHEREAS, Section 91 of RA No. 12009 mandates that the Government Procurement
Policy Board (GPPB) shall be the central body that sets strategic direction and makes policy
decisions regarding all matters affecting public procurement, having due regard to the country's
regional and international obligations, and is tasked to lead the nation's efforts in advancing public
procurement reforms in accordance with the Act;
WHEREAS, Section 91 of RA No. 12009 and its IRR authorizes the GPPB to formulate
public procurement policies, rules and regulations, and amend the IRR, whenever necessary;
WHEREAS, Sections 7.1 and 7.2. of the IRR of RA No. 12009 direct that all procurement
shall be undertaken with proper and sufficient planning and preparation to ensure sound
procurement decisions which include the conduct of supply positioning, analysis of available
modes of procurement, risk management, and disposal procedures and that a procurement
strategy that includes fit-for-purpose and proportional approaches shall be implemented by
Procuring Entities (PEs);
WHEREAS, Section 26.1 of the IRR of RA No. 12009 allows PEs to adopt any of the modes
of procurement consistent with the fit-for-purpose procurement approach to provide the most
suitable mechanism or strategy designed to address the specific needs of the PE and each
project, while promoting flexibility and responsiveness to different conditions and scenarios based
on a variety of factors or situations;
WHEREAS, Section 35 of RA No.

chunks.section: Preliminary
chunks.text:
12009, in relation to Section 35.2 of its IRR, provides that
Negotiated Procurement - Emergency Cases (Emergency Procurement) is one of the instances
where a PE may directly negotiate a contract with a legally, technically, and financially capable
supplier, contractor, or consultant in any of the following cases: (a) imminent danger to life or
property during a state of calamity; (b) when time is of the essence arising from natural or
man-made calamities; or (c) other causes where immediate action is necessary to prevent
damage to or loss of life or property, or to restore vital public services, infrastructure facilities and
other public utilities;
WHEREAS, Section 35.2 of the IRR further provides that the instances or situations where
the foregoing conditions may be applied include the provision of immediate response and initial
recovery steps to avoid loss of life, injury, disease and other negative effects on human, physical,
mental and social well-being, together with damage to property, destruction of assets, loss of
services, social and economic disruption and environmental degradation;
WHEREAS, it is the declared policy of the State, under RA No. 10121 or the "Philippine
Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010", to adopt a disaster risk reduction and
management approach that is holistic, comprehensive, integrated, and proactive in lessening the
socioeconomic and environmental impacts of disasters and to provide maximum care, assistance
and services to people affected by disaster, implement emergency rehabilitation projects to lessen
the impact of disaster, and facilitate resumption of normal social and economic activities;
GPPB Resolution No. 17-2026 dated 14 August 2026 Page 2 of 10
WHEREAS, RA No.

chunks.section: Preliminary
chunks.text:
12287 or the "Declaration of State of Imminent Disaster Act" empowers
the President of the Philippines and the local chief executives to declare a State of Imminent
Disaster anywhere nationwide and in their jurisdictions, respectively, that will allow national
government agencies and local government units, specifically the National, Regional, and Local
DRRM Councils, to use national and local resources and mechanisms to implement anticipatory
actions that will reduce the adverse humanitarian and other impacts of a forecasted hazard before
it occurs, or before its most acute impacts are felt, such as the (a) procurement, mobilization,
strategical prepositioning, and distribution food and non-food items to the forecasted affected
population; (b) implementation of a social amelioration program for the indigent and most
vulnerable members of the population; (c) implementation of contingency plans to mitigate
damage to agricultural products and food supply; and (d) provision of technical and advisory
assistance for the management, control, and reduction of immediate threats to public health and
safety;
WHEREAS, on 9 March, 20 March, and 6 April 2020, respectively, the GPPB issued
Resolution Nos.

chunks.section: Preliminary
chunks.text:
03-2020, 05-2020, and 06-2020 adopting efficient, effective, and expedient
procurement procedures during the COVID-19 State of Public Health Emergency;
WHEREAS, the Philippines has successfully implemented five (5) successive Catastrophe
Deferred Drawdown Option (Cat DDO) operations with the World Bank since 2011, a global
success story in linking policy reforms with disaster risk financing, enabling the Government to
rapidly mobilize financial resources during major disasters and emergencies;
WHEREAS, the World Bank Philippines is preparing the Policy Matrix for the Sixth
Philippines Disaster Risk Management and Climate Development Policy Loan (DPL) with a
Catastrophe-Deferred Drawdown Option (Cat DDO 6), a flagship initiative designed to strengthen
the Philippines' disaster resilience through policy reforms that enhance government preparedness
and response, while providing immediate access to contingent financing following the declaration
of a state of calamity or public health emergency;
WHEREAS, a Technical Working Group (TWG) Meeting for the Sixth Philippines Disaster
Risk Management (DRM) and Climate DPL with CAT-DDO Appraisal Mission was held on
17 June and 29 July 2026, presided over by Department of Finance and attended by
representatives of concerned government agencies, including the Department of the Interior and
Local Government (DILG), the Department of Budget and Management, the Office of Civil
Defense (OCD), the GPPB-Technical Support Office (GPPB-TSO), and the World Bank, to
discuss strategies for streamlining procurement of priority goods and services needed for disaster
preparedness and response;
WHEREAS, pursuant to the foregoing, the GPPB-TSO prepared and drafted the Guidelines
on the Procurement for Disaster Preparedness, Anticipatory Measures, and Disaster-Related
Mitigation Response, Relief, Recovery, Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Other Activities,
Measures, Interventions and Efforts to Protect Lives, Property, Vital Public Services,
Infrastructure Facilities and Other Public Utilities (Guidelines);
WHEREAS, the draft Guidelines were presented to the Inter-Agency Technical Working
Group (IATWG) on its 7th Meeting held on 11 August 2026, for discussion, during which resource
persons from the Department of Agriculture, Department of Health, Department of Social Welfare
and Development, OCD, Philippine Coast Guard, and Quezon City

chunks.section: Preliminary
chunks.text:
and Makati City local
government units were present upon the GPPB-TSO's invitation to provide inputs, comments, or
recommendations pursuant to GPPB Resolution No. 13-2026. The above resource persons
participated in the discussion and provided their inputs and recommendations which were
considered into the draft Guidelines;
WHEREAS, after further review of the proposed Guidelines, the IATWG resolved to endorse
the proposed Guidelines to the GPPB for its consideration and approval;
WHEREAS, the GPPB-TSO during the 5th GPPB Meeting held on 14 August 2026,
presented to the Board the features of the proposed Guidelines, as follows:

chunks.section: Preliminary
chunks.text:
GPPB Resolution No. 17-2026 dated 14 August 2026 Page 3 of 10
1. It covers procurement planning strategies for disaster-preparedness, to wit:
(a) strengthen procurement planning and pre-disaster preparation by requiring PEs to
identify disaster-related requirements, undertake Pre-Disaster Risk Assessment, and
plan for the procurement of Goods, Infrastructure Projects, and Consulting Services
needed for disaster preparedness and response; (b) promote the use of appropriate
procurement strategies, including Early Procurement Activities and Framework
Agreements, to facilitate timely implementation, establish advance procurement
arrangements, and ensure supply security and flexibility; and (c) allow PEs to adopt
the procurement modality best suited to their needs under the Fit-for-Purpose
approach, subject to Market Scoping and applicable rules;
2. It provides for specific rules designed to streamline the use of Emergency
Procurement, including its application to anticipatory actions upon the issuance of a
State of Imminent Disaster such as: (a) rationalization of documentary requirements
by allowing, among others, the use of valid documents previously submitted by
Suppliers, the submission of documents through electronic means, and the
acceptance of electronic notarization, while permitting certain documentary
deficiencies to be completed after award but before payment; and (b) refinement of
the procurement process through simplified compliance documentation, appropriate
delegation of authority, immediate evaluation and negotiation, and expedited approval
and award procedures;
3. It establishes safeguards governing the use of Emergency Procurement by:
(a) providing the proportionality rule between the time element, quantity, volume, or
scope of the procurement; (b) requiring a Suppliers List that will be publicly posted;
(c) guidance on price negotiation to determine reasonableness of price; and
(d) administrative measure against price gouging, bid rigging, collusion, and other
fraudulent practices; and
4.

chunks.section: Preliminary
chunks.text:
Emphasize the accountability and transparency in the procurement process by
including contract implementation rules, including warranty, performance security
where applicable, monitoring of contract compliance, and the imposition of appropriate
penalties or sanctions for delay or non-compliance, as well as prescribing standard
forms and templates to facilitate the uniform and expeditious conduct of Emergency
Procurement.

chunks.section: Section 35.2.4 - OF THIS IRR
chunks.text:
WHEREAS, during the discussion of the proposed guidelines in the 5th GPPB meeting, the
Department of Public Works and Highways, Department of National Defense, DILG, Procurement
Service - DBM (PS-DBM), and the Private Sector Representative expressed their support
therefor, particularly on the Guidelines' objective of facilitating timely, proactive, effective and
responsive procurement interventions for disaster preparedness and emergency response;
WHEREAS, PS-DBM representative clarified that under the current PhilGEPS 1.5 system,
the Suppliers List, Notice of Award (NOA) or contracts cannot be posted if the supplier is not
registered in PhilGEPS. However, this functionality is already being considered under the Terms
of Reference for the Phase 2 development of the modernized PhilGEPS (mPhilGEPS) which will
allow awards to be recognized by the system and posted even if the supplier is not yet registered
in PhilGEPS. The PS-DBM further committed to include this requirement in the Phase 2
development of mPhilGEPS, consistent with other applicable GPPB guidelines;
WHEREAS, the GPPB noted that the BAC Secretariat must post a copy of the Suppliers
List, NOA, and contract on the PE's website and PhilGEPS, and accordingly directed PhilGEPS,
in view of the latter's manifestation of the current inadequate posting functionality on the PhilGEPs
website, to ensure the timely development of a central open-data submission and posting portal
where said information will be posted for transparency and accountability;
WHEREAS, the GPPB Chairperson additionally required further refinements to the
Emergency Procurement Compliance form to ensure that only the necessary and relevant
documents will be required and to include some parameters in requiring performance security;
WHEREAS, the GPPB, after thorough deliberation and inputs from the Members of the
Board, resolved to approve the proposed Guidelines including the related amendments to the IRR
of RA No. 12009, specifically Section 35.2 and its subsections and Section 100.1 as well as the
newly added Section 35.2.4;
NOW, THEREFORE, for and in consideration of the foregoing, WE, the Members of the
GOVERNMENT PROCUREMENT POLICY BOARD, by virtue of the powers vested on US by
law, hereby RESOLVE to confirm, adopt, and approve, as WE hereby:

chunks.text:
Page 1 of 14
CIRCULAR NO. 08-2026
To
:
Heads of Departments, Bureaus, Offices, Agencies of the
National Government; State Universities and Colleges;
Government-Owned
or
Controlled
Corporations;
Government Financial Institutions; Local Government Units
Subject
:
Guidelines on the Procurement for Disaster Preparedness,
Anticipatory Measures, and Disaster-Related Mitigation Response,
Relief, Recovery, Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Other Activities,
Measures, Interventions and Efforts to Protect Lives, Property, Vital
Public Services, Infrastructure Facilities and Other Public Utilities
1.0
POLICY STATEMENT
1.1.
The Government recognizes the strategic role of procurement in the
achievement of a holistic, integrated, efficient and proactive disaster risk
reduction and management program across all levels of governance. In
particular, the Government's disaster preparedness and response during
a State of Calamity, and a State of Imminent Disaster, under Republic
Act (RA) No. 101211 and under RA No. 12287,2 respectively is anchored
on timely, responsive and effective procurement interventions.
1.2.
Relatedly, the fit-for-purpose approach under RA No. 12009 or the New
Government Procurement Act that enables Procuring Entities (PEs)3 to
develop their requirements, choose the procurement modality and
implement contracts that are reasonably proportional to their needs and
circumstances.4 This includes the procurement for disaster
preparedness, anticipatory measures, and disaster-related mitigation
response, relief, recovery, rehabilitation, reconstruction, and other
activities, measures, interventions and efforts to protect lives, property,
vital public services, infrastructure facilities and other public utilities.
1.3.
The need for agility, urgency and proactiveness in the procurement for
disaster-related requirements is nonetheless balanced by the equal need
1 The "Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010."
2 The "Declaration of State of Imminent Disaster Act."
3 Procuring Entity refers to any branch, department, bureau, office, agency, or instrumentality of the government, including
SUCs, GOCCs, GFIs, and LGUs procuring Goods, Infrastructure Projects, and Consulting Services
4 Section 7, RA No. 12009

chunks.section: Annex A - of GPPB Resolution No. 17-2026 dated 14 August 2026
chunks.text:
Page 2 of 14
for Proportionality in procurement strategies and interventions as well
as full disclosure controls under the principle of Transparency.5
2.0
PURPOSE
These Guidelines shall govern the procurement for disaster
preparedness, anticipatory measures, and disaster-related mitigation
response, relief, recovery, rehabilitation, reconstruction, and other
activities, measures, interventions and efforts to protect lives, property,
vital public services, infrastructure facilities and other public utilities.
In particular, it shall provide the rules for Negotiated Procurement,
Emergency Cases under Section 35 (b) of RA No. 12009 and Section
35.2 of the IRR of RA 12009.
3.0
DEFINITION OF TERMS
a.
Anticipatory Action refers to action taken to reduce the adverse
humanitarian and other impacts of a forecasted hazard before it occurs,
or before its most acute impacts are felt. It is performed by any
individual, organization, or concerned government agency to mitigate a
disaster's impact on people, animals, and properties that are likely to
be affected.6
b.
Declaration of a State of Imminent Disaster refers to the
declaration made in anticipation of a highly probable disaster with
projected catastrophic impacts based on forecast and on the results of
pre-disaster risk assessment to supplement national and local resources
in preventing or mitigating damages and losses.7
c.
Disaster refers to a serious disruption of the functioning of a
community or a society involving widespread human, material,
economic or environmental losses and impacts, which exceeds the
ability of the affected community or society to cope using its own
resources.8
d.
Pre-Disaster Risk Assessment refers to the process of evaluating a
hazard's level of risk given the degree of exposure and vulnerability in
a specific area. It presents the possible impacts on the people, animals,
production capacities, environmental services, and properties and
serves as basis to determine the appropriate level of response actions
from the national government agencies down to LGUs.9
5 Transparency in the procurement process by providing access to all related information in accordance with open contracting
practice that enables the disclosure of data and facilities information sharing related to all stages of procurement. Section 3(a)
of the IRR of RA 12009
6 Section 3(a), RA No. 12287
7 Section 3 (c), RA No.

chunks.section: Annex A - of GPPB Resolution No. 17-2026 dated 14 August 2026
chunks.text:
Page 3 of 14
e.
State of Calamity refers to a condition involving mass casualty and/or
major damages to property, disruption of means of livelihoods, roads
and normal way of life of people in the affected areas as a result of the
occurrence of natural or human-induced hazard.10
f.
Suppliers refer to manufacturers, distributors, resellers, contractors,
or consultants.
4.0
SCOPE AND COVERAGE
4.1
These Guidelines shall apply to:
a. PEs of all branches and instrumentalities of the National Government,
its departments, bureaus, offices and agencies, including State
Universities and Colleges (SUCs), Government-Owned or Controlled
Corporations (GOCCs), Government Financial Institutions (GFIs), and
Local Government Units (LGUs); and
b. all types of procurement, whether Goods, Infrastructure Projects and
Consulting Services.

chunks.section: Section 5.0 - GENERAL GUIDELINES
chunks.text:
5.1
RA No. 1200911 decreed a whole Article on Strategic Procurement
Planning and Budgeting Linkage to ensure that all procurement projects
are undertaken with proper and sufficient planning and preparation to
ensure sound procurement decisions. This includes the conduct of
relevant market scoping, supply positioning, analysis of available
procurement modalities, risk management, and disposal procedures as
may be applicable.12
5.2
PEs shall likewise adopt a procurement strategy that includes fit-for-
purpose and proportional approaches, considers the whole lifecycle of a
procurement project, including its environmental impact, and aims to
achieve value for money.13
5.3
Among the procurement strategies available is the conduct of Early
Procurement Activities pending the approval of the budget, where PEs
may undertake the procurement activities, short of award. The award
of contract shall be made only upon the approval and effectivity of the
funding source.14 The conduct of Early Procurement Activities gives PEs
a level of comfort and security that their projects will be implemented
10 Section 3 (ll), RA No. 10121
11 The "New Government Procurement Act."
12 Section 7 of RA No. 12009
13 Section 7, 2nd Paragraph, RA No. 12009
14 Section 12, RA No. 12009

chunks.section: Annex A - of GPPB Resolution No. 17-2026 dated 14 August 2026
chunks.text:
Page 4 of 14
on time especially disaster-prevention and mitigation projects that are
meant to build resiliency.
5.4
PEs may also benefit from the use of Framework Agreement to expand
the pool of prospective bidders, take advantage of economies of scale,
minimize the administrative burden of conducting separate procurement
activities, and generate time and money savings.15 As it is in the nature
of an option contact, PEs are able to establish a pre-arranged
procurement structure in advance while actual procurements are done
on a needs basis.
5.5
Consistent with the fit-for-purpose approach, PEs may adopt any of the
modalities under Section 26 of RA No. 12009 and its Implementing Rules
and Regulations (IRR) that is best suited to the needs of its procurement
subject to the conduct of Market Scoping as provided under Section 10
of RA 12009 and its IRR.16
5.6
Among the modalities that may be adopted is Negotiated Procurement,
Emergency Cases ("Emergency Procurement") in case of imminent
danger to life or property during a state of calamity, or when time is of
the essence arising from natural or man-made calamities, or where
immediate action is necessary to prevent damage to or loss of life or
property, or to restore vital public services, infrastructure facilities, and
other public utilities.17
5.7
In the case of Infrastructure Projects, the PE has the option to undertake
the project by Administration or in high security risk areas, through the
Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP).
5.8
The Head of Procuring Entity (HoPE)18 may likewise establish a Bids and
Awards Committee dedicated to handling the procurement for disaster
preparedness, anticipatory measures, and disaster and calamity-related
mitigation response, relief, recovery, rehabilitation, reconstruction, and
other activities, measures, interventions and efforts to protect lives,
property, vital public services, infrastructure facilities and other public
utilities. This will create expertise within the PE that will enable rapid
response, mitigating the incidence of delay due to uncertainty in action
or confusion under pressure.
15 Section 16, RA No.

5.9
Similarly, in order to ensure the timely conduct of procurement activities
related to the happening of disasters, as well as when time is of the
essence, the HoPE may delegate to the End-User or Implementing Unit19
or any other appropriate bureau, committee or procuring unit the
authority to directly negotiate with a legally, technically, and financially
capable Supplier under Emergency Procurement or conduct other
applicable modes of procurement20 under Section 26 of RA No. 12009
and its IRR. Moreover, a pre-defined delegation of authority in the above
cases where immediate response is demanded enhances institutional
integrity and avoids abuse of discretion.

chunks.section: Section 6.0 - PRE-DISASTER PREPARATION
chunks.text:
6.1
End-User or Implementing Units shall consider all the requirements
needed for the implementation of policies, plans, actions and measures
pertaining to all aspects of disaster preparedness, risk reduction and
management. For this purpose, End-User or Implementing Units are
encouraged to carry out Pre-Disaster Risk Assessment to anticipate
needs arising from possible disasters and plan for procurements needed
for disaster preparedness and response.
6.2
In the conduct of procurement for disaster preparedness, anticipatory
measures, and disaster-related mitigation response, relief, recovery,
rehabilitation,
reconstruction
and
other
activities,
measures,
interventions and efforts to protect lives, property, vital public services,
infrastructure facilities and other public utilities, PEs may adopt any of
the applicable procurement modalities under Section 26 of RA No. 12009
and its IRR. This includes undertaking early procurement activities,
short of award subject to applicable guidelines.
6.3
An important aspect of pre-disaster preparation is the determination of
the Goods21, Infrastructure Projects22 and Consulting Services23 that may
be needed during a State of Calamity or a State of Imminent Disaster.
The End-User or Implementing Unit should consider how it may benefit
19 End-User or Implementing Unit refers to the employee or organic office within the organization of the Procuring Entity that
identifies, plans, prepares, designs, and implements the procurement project based on the requirements or needs of the
agency in accordance with its mandate

21 Goods refers to all items, supplies, materials, and general support services, except Consulting Services and Infrastructure
Projects, which may be needed in the transaction of public businesses or in the pursuit of any government undertaking, project
or activity, whether in the nature of equipment, furniture, stationery, materials, for construction, or personal property of any
kind, including non-personal or contractual services such as the repair and maintenance of equipment and furniture, as well as
trucking, hauling, janitorial, security, and related or analogous services, as well as procurement of materials and supplies
provided by the Procuring Entity for such services
22 Infrastructur

of roads and bridges, railways, airports, seaports, communication facilities, civil works components of information technology

protection, energy/power and electrification facilities, national buildings, school buildings, hospital buildings, and other related
